what.title: What you can do here
what.text: Search for a word or sentence of any course (the target text, a meaning or an id from a report), open it and change its text, its meaning or the other accepted answers, hide an exercise that is wrong as a whole, or record its sound again.

job.title: Who applies a correction
job.text: Saving puts the correction in a queue. The content job on this server applies one at a time, usually within a minute: it changes the lesson source, rebuilds the lessons, checks the word list and the ids, makes new recordings when the text changed, runs the tests, saves a version in the history and reloads the app without logging anyone out. If any step fails, everything is put back and History says why. No AI is involved.

audio.title: Recordings
audio.text: Changing the text makes its recordings again automatically. Record again (under the recording) makes a new take of the same text: you hear the old and the new one and keep one. The Listen check shows how good the recordings are and serves the new ones first.

undo.title: Undo
undo.text: History lists every correction with its status. An applied correction can be undone; the undo goes through the same job.

reports.title: The children's reports
reports.text: A report in the Inbox opens the correction page for its word or sentence. When the correction is applied the report closes and the child is thanked.

limits.title: What needs a developer
limits.text: New words, sentences, lessons or units, a new level, and pronunciation entries are authoring work: a developer makes them on the server, with the authoring tools (docs/developer/content.md), never the running app.

listen.title: Listen check
listen.intro: Listen to one recording at a time, exactly as learners hear it, and say whether it is right. Short sittings are fine: the check carries on where it stopped. The table below shows how good the recordings are; it stays up to date by itself.
listen.again: This clip was marked Bad and has been rendered again: listen once more.
listen.queue: Waiting for a new rendering: {waiting} · rendered again, to hear once more: {again} · fixed: {fixed}
listen.statsAbout: Per language and kind of clip: how many clips there are, how many were heard and how many of those were bad. "At most" is the 95 % upper bound on the share of bad clips (with none bad: 3 divided by the clips heard), and the line under it applies it to all clips of that kind.
listen.queueAbout: Open a clip to record it again (a new take, checked automatically; you choose which one to keep).
listen.needsLexicon: Marked Bad for its pronunciation: a new take seldom helps. It needs an entry in the pronunciation list, made by a developer on the server (docs/developer/audio.md).

what.title: What you hear
what.text: Each clip is one of the recordings the app plays to learners, that exact file: a word or short phrase, a sentence, or a sentence of a reading text or dialogue, at normal or slow speed. Everything runs on this server; no AI and no internet service is involved.

picked.title: How clips are picked
picked.text: The server picks the next clip: first a clip marked Bad that was recorded again (to hear once more), then a new recording nobody has heard yet, then a random one — two times in three a sentence, otherwise a word or short phrase, in a random language. A recording is never served twice. Stop whenever you like: only your verdicts are saved, so the next sitting carries on.

verdict.title: Your verdict
verdict.text: OK or Bad is saved with that exact recording and the admin who gave it. Mark it Bad for babble, a cut-off start or end, a wrong word or a wrong pronunciation; a reason and a note help whoever fixes it. When a recording is replaced, the verdict stays with the old file and the new one waits to be heard.

bad.title: What happens to a Bad clip
bad.text: Nothing happens by itself: it goes to the fix queue below, with the reason and the note given. Open it: Heard OK now marks this very recording OK (it sounded fine after all), and it leaves the queue. Record again makes a new take of that one recording (the same voice, another random variation), measured by the automatic audio check; you hear Old (the recording in use) and New and choose. Keep new puts it in use at once (saved in the version history), and it comes back here to be heard. Keep old keeps the recording in use and marks it heard OK. Neither — try again throws the new take away and keeps the clip in the queue, to record again later. No developer is needed for this.

pronunciation.title: A wrong pronunciation
pronunciation.text: A new take of the same spelling usually says a word the same way. A wrong pronunciation is fixed with an entry in the pronunciation list (content/src/<language>/pronunciations.yaml: how the voice must say the word), written by a developer on the server, with the authoring tools (docs/developer/audio.md), and then heard here. Such clips stay in the fix queue, marked as needing a pronunciation fix.

machine.title: The automatic audio check
machine.text: npm run audio:check is a script on this server, not an AI. It measures each recording (loudness, length, silences, a second burst of voice) and writes down what an offline speech recognizer hears, and flags recordings that look wrong. It runs after recordings are made and for every Record again. It cannot tell whether a word sounds natural: that is what this page is for.

table.title: The Audio quality table
table.text: Per language, for words and short phrases and for sentences: how many recordings the app has, how many were heard here, how many of those are Bad now, and "at most": with 95 % certainty the share of bad recordings in the whole group is below this number (with none bad: 3 divided by the number heard). The more you hear, the lower it gets. "Rendered again" counts the recordings with a fix of their own (another take, a cut, a pin). The numbers are worked out each time the page opens, so every new recording counts at once.

later.title: Later
later.text: The verdicts stay in the database. Later, a developer on the server can read them and improve what was found (docs/developer/audio.md describes how).

rules.title: What counts as correct
rules.intro: How the app grades answers: one line per rule, with an example. Open a heading, or search. These rules are the same for every learner.
